text:
Jana: Trying to install redwoodctl on a fresh Win11 box via Scoop and hitting a weird PATH/symlink problem. Installer says install succeeded but command not found in WSL (Ubuntu).

Jana: Steps I ran:
- `scoop install redwoodctl`
- `scoop which redwoodctl` -> returns `C:\Users\\Jana\\scoop\\apps\\redwoodctl\x64\\current\\redwoodctl.exe`
- `redwoodctl --version` in PowerShell works, in WSL it does not. :confused:

matt: Scoop drops the exe in Windows FS, WSL won't see it unless PATH is shared or you symlink into /usr/local/bin. Did you add a shim?

Jana: I tried `ln -s /mnt/c/Users/Jana/scoop/apps/redwoodctl/x64/current/redwoodctl.exe /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` but `ln` fails (permission denied). Also PowerShell blocked the remote script once earlier due to execution policy.

ashwin: Two things here: 1) Windows exec policy can block the bootstrap if you used the installer script. 2) WSL can't run Windows executables without `wslpath` translation for symlinks.

leah: Workaround I use: install the standalone zip to a shared folder and create a small wrapper bash script in /usr/local/bin that calls `/mnt/c/Users/you/path/redwoodctl.exe "$@"`. No symlink needed.

Jana: Hmm ok. Also when I try `redwoodctl auth login` inside WSL it opens the browser on Windows, but browser returns an error page: "invalid redirect". Headless dev flow is blocked for me. Anyone seen that?

ashwin: Yep. Browser flow + WSL where the CLI launches Windows browser sometimes breaks because the callback expects localhost on WSL network. Use device-code flow: `redwoodctl auth login --device`. That prints a code and a URL you can paste in any browser.

matt: If you need a quick fix for exec policy (only if you're comfortable): run PowerShell as admin and `Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine`. That lets the installer script run. But call it out in the onboarding docs with a warning.

Jana: Device flow worked! But token ended up saved to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\redwood\\profiles.json`. WSL can't read that path by default unless I mount it. I expected token to land in `~/.redwood/profiles.json` when running inside WSL.

rob: That's a legit DX bug: installer/CLI chooses Windows home path when invoked in WSL if the binary is a Windows exe. File issue? :+1:

leah: Filed as TICKET-4352 (devex) with reproduction steps and suggested fix: if running under WSL (detect via `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` env) prefer `$HOME/.redwood` store or mirror creds to both places.

dev-tools-bot: New ticket created: TICKET-4352 — CLI: credential file written to Windows path when running under WSL. Assigned to @ashwin.

ashwin: I pushed a small patch that prefers a unix-style config dir when `uname` shows Linux and `/proc/version` contains "Microsoft". PR link: https://git.redwood.internal/pulls/2987 (internal).

Jana: Verified patched CLI from my dev build. `redwoodctl auth login --device` now writes to `~/.redwood/profiles.json` in WSL. Device flow + wrapper script combo works for me. Thanks everyone :rocket:

matt: Can we add a note in the Windows install doc: "If you install the Windows binary and use WSL, prefer the device flow or install the Linux binary inside WSL to avoid credential path mismatch"?

leah: Yep, adding to onboarding checklist and created a short snippet to show wrapper script:```bash
#!/bin/bash
/mnt/c/Users/jana/scoop/apps/redwoodctl/x64/current/redwoodctl.exe "$@"
```

Jana: Saved that. One more tiny request: make `redwoodctl install --force-symlink` create a WSL-friendly shim when run inside WSL. If we can auto-detect and offer to place a small bash wrapper, that'll cut support noise.

ashwin: Good idea. I'll add it to the PR (option flag and auto-detect). Won't be default unless user consents.

Jana: Great. Closing my blocker for the day. Thanks :smile:
